items.headline: Six Spanish biotech startups to watch in 2026
items.preview: The Spanish biotech ecosystem is expanding rapidly, with significant funding and new startups emerging.
items.article:
The 2025 AseBio Report highlights a growing Spanish biotech sector, with 1,119 companies and a 125% increase in funding to €408 million. This growth is marked by the emergence of innovative startups like Telum Therapeutics, Integra Therapeutics, and others, each focusing on unique therapeutic areas such as antimicrobial therapies and gene editing. 
Why this matters: These startups represent a new wave of drug developers in Spain, potentially transforming the landscape of biotechnology and healthcare through their innovative approaches and technologies.

items.headline: Engineered mini CRISPR enzyme gets a 60-fold power boost for gene editing
items.preview: A newly engineered CRISPR enzyme shows significant improvements in gene editing efficiency.
items.article:
Researchers have transformed the compact CRISPR nuclease CgCas12n into a high-performance genome-editing tool, achieving up to 60 times higher editing efficiency than its wild-type form. This advancement is crucial for overcoming delivery challenges in gene therapy, particularly with adeno-associated virus vectors. 
Why this matters: The enhanced performance of CgCas12n could lead to more effective and accessible gene editing applications, particularly in therapeutic contexts where precision and efficiency are paramount.

items.headline: Approved Metabolism Drugs Rescue Disease Signs in SMA Mice
items.preview: Three approved drugs show promise in improving symptoms of spinal muscular atrophy in mice.
items.article:
A study has demonstrated that pioglitazone, melatonin, and insulin can improve various disease phenotypes in a mouse model of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). These drugs target metabolic dysfunctions associated with SMA, suggesting a need for metabolic therapies alongside existing treatments. 
Why this matters: This research highlights the potential for repurposing approved drugs to address metabolic aspects of SMA, which could enhance treatment options for patients suffering from this debilitating condition.

items.headline: A developmental single-cell atlas of the Drosophila visual system glia reveals cell type diversification and subcellular mRNA compartmentalization
items.preview: A comprehensive study of Drosophila glial cells provides insights into their development and function.
items.article:
This research presents a detailed transcriptomic analysis of glial cells in the Drosophila visual system, revealing their diversification and developmental trajectories. The study identifies new genetic markers and highlights the distinct mRNA localization in glial cell bodies and processes. 
Why this matters: Understanding glial cell development and function is crucial for insights into nervous system health and disease, potentially informing therapeutic strategies for neurological disorders.

items.headline: Kodiak skyrockets on positive study data for 2 eye drugs
items.preview: Kodiak Sciences reports successful Phase 3 trial results for its macular degeneration drugs.
items.article:
Shares of Kodiak Sciences surged after the company announced that its drugs Zenkuda and tabirafusp alfa tedromer matched the efficacy of Regeneron's Eylea in a Phase 3 trial. The individualized dosing strategy allowed for longer intervals between injections, enhancing patient convenience. 
Why this matters: The positive trial results could lead to FDA approvals, offering new treatment options for age-related macular degeneration and potentially transforming patient care in ophthalmology.
